subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Why are vitamin A and Vitamin C essential to us? Give their important sources.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Vitamin A
lines: Function: needed for normal vision, for
protein synthesis, and for normal growth of
Sources: fish liver oil, carrots, butter
steps.why: Vitamin A is used to make the light-sensitive pigment of the eye, which is why the first sign of shortage shows in vision. It is fat soluble, so the sources listed are oily or fatty foods, together with carrots, which supply the orange pigment the body converts into it.
common_mistakes: Giving scurvy as the deficiency of vitamin A. Scurvy belongs to vitamin C; vitamin A gives night blindness.
Writing only the sources. The question asks why the vitamin is essential, so the function is needed too.
steps.memory_tip: A is for the eye: fish liver oil and carrots, night blindness if short.
steps.margin_note: Two parts per vitamin: what it does, and where it comes from. Head each one with the vitamin's letter.

steps.label: Vitamin C

lines.text: Vitamin C: collagen; lack causes scurvy

lines: Function: needed for the synthesis of
collagen, the protein of skin, gums and
Sources: citrus fruits, amla, green leafy
steps.why: Collagen cannot be made properly without vitamin C, and collagen holds skin, gums and blood vessel walls together, so a shortage shows as bleeding gums and slow healing, which is scurvy. Vitamin C is water soluble and is not stored, so it has to be taken regularly.
common_mistakes: Naming rickets for vitamin C. Rickets is the vitamin D deficiency; vitamin C gives scurvy.
Calling vitamin C fat soluble. It is water soluble, and so it is not stored in the body.
steps.memory_tip: C makes collagen; without it, scurvy.
steps.margin_note: Name the disease each vitamin prevents even though the question does not ask. It is the fastest way to show the function.

insider_note: Two vitamins, two things each: function and source. The examiner is counting four items, so lay them out as four labelled lines.
